name: KATRIN
summary: KATRIN measures the electron-antineutrino mass from the tritium beta-decay endpoint at Karlsruhe. Its large electrostatic spectrometer resolves the small spectral distortion associated with a nonzero neutrino mass.
detection_principle: A windowless gaseous tritium source supplies beta electrons. Magnetic transport guides them into a MAC-E filter, which scans the integrated electron spectrum close to its 18.6 keV endpoint.

status.label: Multiple stages
status.evidence: The endpoint neutrino-mass campaign reached 1000 measurement days and was followed by commissioning of TRISTAN, reported in May 2026. The published 0.45 eV/c2 mass bound uses the earlier 259-day sample.

collaboration.name: KATRIN Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

phases.name: Endpoint active-neutrino-mass campaign
phases.description: Precision tritium endpoint measurements; complete accumulated data remain subject to analysis

phases.name: TRISTAN sterile-neutrino upgrade
phases.description: Named high-rate detector upgrade; separate programme dossier provided

results.summary: Five measurement campaigns yielded the published 0.45 eV/c2 limit; this is an upper bound, not a measured mass.

science_scope: This is a laboratory kinematic measurement of the effective electron-flavour neutrino mass. Its observable differs from the effective Majorana mass in neutrinoless double-beta decay and the sum of neutrino masses inferred from cosmology.
